transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

I’ve been having these really strong beliefs that people are watching me and out to get me, even when I know it sounds strange. It’s gotten worse over the past few months and I’m starting to feel really unsafe and confused, so I thought I should get help.

Around the time these beliefs started or got worse, have you had any periods lasting several days where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep, were more talkative, or acted in ways that were very out of character for you?
I don’t think so. I’ve mostly felt tired and worn down, not extra energetic or anything like that.
How long have you been experiencing these beliefs and feeling unsafe—would you say it’s been more like days to weeks, or has it been going on for several months or longer without really going away?
It’s been going on for several months without really going away. The feeling of being unsafe has been there that whole time, but in the last month or so the beliefs have gotten a lot more intense.

Apart from these beliefs that people are watching you or out to get you, have you noticed things like hearing voices when no one is there, seeing things others don’t see, or your thoughts feeling jumbled or hard to organize?

Yeah, I’ve been hearing voices pretty often, like people commenting on what I’m doing or saying my name when no one is there. I don’t really see things that aren’t there, but my thoughts feel kind of foggy and sometimes it’s hard to keep a straight line in a conversation.

Over the past several months, have you noticed changes like losing motivation, withdrawing from friends or activities, neglecting self-care, or having trouble working or studying compared to how you used to be?

Yeah, a lot. I barely see my friends anymore and I’ve stopped doing hobbies I used to enjoy, and it’s been really hard to keep up with work and even basic things like showering regularly or keeping my place clean.

Have you been using any substances like cannabis, alcohol, stimulants (such as cocaine or meth), or hallucinogens in the past year, and if so, did your symptoms start or worsen around the times you used them or soon after stopping?

I drink a little alcohol on weekends, like a couple of beers, but nothing heavy, and I don’t really use other drugs. I didn’t notice any clear connection between drinking and when these symptoms started or got worse.
Thinking back to when these symptoms first began, did they come on very suddenly over a few days with a big, dramatic change, or did they build up more gradually over weeks to months?
They built up more gradually over weeks to months. The fear and sense of being watched kind of crept in and slowly got stronger, rather than everything changing all at once.

Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt very down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, along with losing interest in things you usually enjoy or having major changes in sleep or appetite?

Yeah, for about the last two months I’ve felt really low almost all day, pretty much every day, and I don’t really enjoy anything anymore. My appetite’s dropped a lot and I’ve lost some weight, and it’s hard to concentrate on things like reading or even following TV.

Thinking back over the past several months, have there been times when the suspicious beliefs and voices were still happening even though your mood was not especially depressed, or have these psychotic symptoms only been present during the period when you’ve been feeling very low?

Yeah, there was a stretch before I got this depressed where the suspicious thoughts and the voices were already there, but my mood wasn’t as low as it is now. For at least a few weeks I still felt kind of “okay” mood‑wise, just anxious, while the paranoia and voices were happening.

Have you ever had similar problems with paranoia, hearing voices, or feeling very withdrawn at any earlier time in your life, and how old were you when these kinds of symptoms first started, even if they were milder then?

I think this is the first time it’s been this bad, with the paranoia and voices this constant. Looking back, I might have had milder suspicious thoughts and feeling kind of detached in my early twenties, but nothing that really stood out or interfered with my life like this.

Therefore, F20.0 remains a leading candidate and F32.3 is added as a differential diagnosis. Further questioning is needed to distinguish definitively, so the list has expanded and is_final remains false.

There were no previous candidates provided, so this is an initial broad differential; further questioning is needed about mood symptoms, duration, functional impact, hallucinations, thought disorder, substance use, medical history, and family history.

The patient continues to report long-standing persecutory beliefs (people watching and out to get them) over several months, which is consistent with both candidates. However, they now clearly describe frequent auditory experiences of voices commenting on their actions and calling their name, plus some thought disorganization ("foggy" thinking, difficulty keeping a straight line in conversation). The presence of persistent hallucinations and thought disorder makes a purely persistent delusional disorder less likely and shifts the balance toward schizophrenia, but does not completely rule out F22.0 because we still need more detailed information about the full symptom profile, negative symptoms, functional decline, and any mood episodes. Therefore, the candidate list remains the same, but the relative likelihood of schizophrenia has increased. Further questioning is still needed, so this is not final.

inference_history.note: Previously the candidates were [F22.0, F20.0]. The patient describes several months of persistent persecutory beliefs accompanied by clear auditory hallucinations (voices commenting, saying their name), thought disorganization (foggy thinking, difficulty maintaining a line of conversation), and marked negative symptoms (social withdrawal, loss of motivation, neglect of self-care, occupational decline). This constellation strongly supports a schizophrenia-spectrum disorder with prominent positive and negative symptoms rather than a persistent delusional disorder, which by definition should not have this level of hallucinations or negative symptoms. There is no history suggestive of mood episodes (no manic symptoms, primarily tired and worn down), making a primary mood disorder with psychotic features less likely. Thus F22.0 becomes unlikely and is removed, leaving F20.0 as the current candidate. Further questioning is still needed about duration in total, functional decline course, substance use, medical causes, and mood symptoms, so this is not yet final.

Because the total duration is described as "several months" rather than clearly more than 6 months, an acute psychotic disorder with predominant paranoid features remains a secondary possibility until the exact timeline (onset of first psychotic symptoms vs. current evaluation) is clarified. Thus the current candidates are a chronic primary psychotic disorder and an acute psychotic disorder with prominent paranoid symptoms. Further clarification of exact duration, premorbid functioning, and any prodromal phase is needed, so this is not yet final.

This temporal pattern—psychosis occurring outside of and preceding the depressive episode—argues against a primary severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms as the main diagnosis, and is more consistent with a primary psychotic disorder. (3) There is no evidence of manic or hypomanic episodes, and no substance trigger. Given these points, a primary schizophrenia‑spectrum disorder remains the leading possibility, so F20.0 is retained and F32.3 is removed as a primary candidate (though depressive symptoms can be comorbid or part of the course). Further questioning is still needed about duration, functional decline, and other domains, so the diagnosis is not yet final.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has had several months of prominent persecutory delusions and third-person auditory hallucinations, with gradual onset, thought disorganization (foggy, hard to keep a straight line), and marked negative symptoms (social withdrawal, loss of motivation, neglect of self-care) leading to functional decline. Psychotic symptoms clearly preceded and are not limited to the current depressive episode, and there is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes or substance use explaining the presentation. This pattern is most consistent with paranoid schizophrenia (F20.0) rather than a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms (F32.3), in which psychosis would be confined to periods of severe depression.
